summary:
Echoes of Space is an interactive digital museum that brings the stories of NASA's forgotten space explorers to life. We developed a web platform where users can explore Earth, Mars and the Moon, discover old rovers, landers and spacecraft, and learn about the missions they were part of.

The platform includes interactive 3D visualisations, a space equipment explorer, mission timelines, scientific discoveries, mission comparisons and quizzes. We also developed an AI Space Historian that answers questions using verified NASA mission records and provides source references.

Our project addresses the challenge of making the history of retired and inactive space equipment more interesting and easier to understand, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. Instead of going through complicated technical information, users can explore missions and discover the science behind them in an interactive way.

Through Echoes of Space, we hope to preserve the stories of these machines, encourage curiosity about space and inspire the next generation to explore science and technology.
details:
Project Details – Echoes of Space

1. What the Project Does

Echoes of Space is an interactive 3D digital museum that preserves and showcases the history of NASA's robotic explorers and lunar equipment. Users can explore Earth, Mars and the Moon, discover forgotten spacecraft, rovers and landers, and learn about the missions and scientific discoveries associated with them.

2. How It Works

The platform brings NASA mission information together in one place and presents it through interactive features.

  • 3D Planetary Exploration: Explore realistic 3D models of Earth, Mars and the Moon.
  • Space Equipment Explorer: Search, filter and explore 12 historical spacecraft and hardware relics.
  • Interactive Hardware Inspector: Examine detailed 3D spacecraft models and their components.
  • Mission Timeline: Follow 24 important milestones in space exploration.
  • Scientific Discoveries Archive: Explore six major scientific discoveries.
  • Mission Comparison: Compare spacecraft, their engineering specifications and instruments.
  • AI Space Historian: Ask questions and receive answers grounded in verified NASA mission records, with source citations.
  • Mission Detective Quiz: Solve five interactive mystery cases and earn NASA Curator Ranks.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space exploration easier and more interesting for students, educators and space enthusiasts. It converts complex technical information into an interactive learning experience, encourages scientific curiosity and helps preserve the history of machines whose missions have ended.

Our aim is to help younger audiences understand not just what NASA explored, but also how these machines contributed to scientific discoveries.

4. Tools and Technologies

Software-based project (No hardware required).

  • 3D Graphics: Three.js (r128)
  • Rendering: WebGL 2.0
  • Frontend: HTML5 and Tailwind CSS
  • Programming: JavaScript
  • Icons: Lucide Icons
  • Data Storage: JSON datasets and browser LocalStorage
  • AI Component: RAG Query Engine / AI Space Historian
  • Modular Architecture: React and TypeScript-ready source

5. Creativity and Innovation

What makes Echoes of Space different is the way it turns forgotten space equipment into something people can actively explore. Instead of presenting mission information as ordinary articles, it combines 3D planetary environments, interactive spacecraft models, historical timelines, scientific discoveries and an AI-based space historian.

The platform also connects individual discoveries back to the spacecraft responsible for them, helping users understand the relationship between engineering and scientific progress.

6. Technical and Educational Factors

The project follows a modular, frontend-first architecture. Its mission data is organised into eight structured datasets containing 12 hardware records, eight historical programs, 22 scientific instruments, six discoveries, 24 timeline milestones and 13 verified NASA source registries.

The platform uses open-source web technologies and browser-based rendering, making it accessible without specialised hardware.

Overall, Echoes of Space aims to turn the forgotten history of space exploration into an experience that people can explore, learn from and remember.
